4:66.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّا كَتَبۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنِ ٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱخۡرُجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِكُم مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فَعَلُواْ مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَشَدَّ تَثۡبِيتࣰ ا
4:66.en: And if We had decreed for them: Lay down your lives or go forth from your dwellings, but few of them would have done it; though if they did what they are exhorted to do it would be better for them, and more strengthening

2:54.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّكُمۡ ظَلَمۡتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ فَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:54.en: And when Moses said unto his people: O my people! Ye have wronged yourselves by your choosing of the calf (for worship) so turn in penitence to your Creator, and kill (the guilty) yourselves. That will be best for you with your Creator and He will relent toward you. Lo! He is the Relenting, the Merciful

47:36.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱۚ وَإِن تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ يُؤۡتِكُمۡ أُجُورَكُمۡ وَلَا يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَكُمۡ
47:36.en: The life of the world is but a sport and a pastime. And if ye believe and ward off (evil). He will give you your wages, and will not ask of you your wordly wealth

47:37.ar: إِن يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمُوهَا فَيُحۡفِكُمۡ تَبۡخَلُواْ وَيُخۡرِجۡ أَضۡغَٰنَكُمۡ
47:37.en: If He should ask it of you and importune you, ye would hoard it, and He would bring to light your (secret) hates

2:185.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:185.en: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of the guidance, and the Criterion (of right and wrong). And whosoever of you is present, let him fast the month, and whosoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast the same) number of other days. Allah desireth for you ease; He desireth not hardship for you; and (He desireth) that ye should complete the period, and that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you, and that peradventure ye may be thankful

22:78.ar: وَجَٰهِدُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَىٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ
22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the endeavour which is His right. He hath chosen you and hath not laid upon you in religion any hardship; the faith of your father Abraham (is yours). He hath named you Muslims of old time and in this (Scripture), that the messenger may be a witness against you, and that ye may be witnesses against mankind. So establish worship, pay the poor-due, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protecting friend. A blessed Patron and a blessed Helper

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast

37:103.en: Then, when they had both surrendered (to Allah), and he had flung him down upon his face

37:104.en: We called unto him: O Abraham

37:105.ar: قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
37:105.en: Thou hast already fulfilled the vision. Lo! thus do We reward the good

37:106.en: Lo! that verily was a clear test

37:107.en: Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim

5JuPYyrlxso.speaker: adnan
5JuPYyrlxso.speaker_note: Single voice speaking as the community's imam; uses his own parenting as an example.
5JuPYyrlxso.title: Hajj: Celebration of the Greatest Submission
5JuPYyrlxso.one_line: Allah could have commanded us to do harmful, senseless things but never did; Eid al-Adha celebrates that mercy and Ibrahim's total submission.
5JuPYyrlxso.summary: Given the week before Eid al-Adha, this khutbah starts from 4:66: had Allah ordered people to kill themselves or leave their homes, few would have obeyed. The sheikh shows that Allah once did give such a command, when the Israelites repented from the golden calf by killing one another, to teach that every other command was for their own good. Surah Muhammad makes the same point about wealth: He asks for 2.5% of stagnant wealth, not all of it. Allah's commands are reasoned and serve our interest, and He adds reward on top, like a loving parent who rewards a child for studying. Then the centrepiece: Ibrahim, the man who questioned everything, receives a command with no visible wisdom and asks nothing. Ismail, a teenager, agrees, Shaytan is stoned three times, and the moment both submit coins the word Muslim. Eid celebrates that Allah never asked this of us. So he challenges those who complain about hijab, alcohol or other limits, and ties submission to standing for justice. In the second khutbah he calls this complaining vanity, as if we were speaking to an equal.

outline.heading: Opening
Had We decreed that they kill themselves
outline.gist: An-Nisa 4:66 states a fact the Quran and the Prophet repeat often: Allah never commanded what harms us, and this season is the time to understand it.

outline.heading: The golden calf and the one useless command
outline.gist: To repent from the calf, the Israelites were ordered to draw swords on one another; Musa begged for the decree to be lifted, and Allah forgave them and brought them back. The lesson: I could have made all My commands like this one, but I didn't.

outline.heading: He did not ask for all your wealth
outline.gist: Surah Muhammad: asking for everything would expose our stinginess, so He asked only for 2.5% of stagnant wealth held for a year. He could have, but He didn't.

outline.heading: Commands reasoned for our interest, with reward added
outline.gist: Every command in the deen has a reason aimed at the creation's best interest. No one obliges Allah to make it so; He chose it, and then added reward on top.

outline.heading: The parent who rewards a child for studying
outline.gist: A parent rewards a child for memorizing Quran and studying, though it benefits only the child, because love aligns the child's interest with reward. Some fathers bluff the opposite, but the goal is the same.

outline.heading: No excuse left: ease, not hardship
outline.gist: Allah treats us the same way, so what argument is left for not following His commands? He wants ease, not hardship, and placed no difficulty in the deen (2:185, 22:78).

outline.heading: Ibrahim's long-awaited son, left far away
outline.gist: Allah could have commanded anything, and these days exist because He didn't. Ibrahim waited many years for a son, left him in a barren valley and visited only by permission, until the boy grew old enough to be useful to him.

outline.heading: The vision that kept returning
outline.gist: Ibrahim sees himself slaughtering his son and wakes terrified, not of the dream but that it may be revelation. He gives it time, and the same vision returns every night, down to the place, until he knows it is a command.

outline.heading: Ibrahim the questioner
outline.gist: Throughout the Quran Ibrahim argues with his father, his people, the star-worshippers and the king, and even asks Allah to show him how He gives life to the dead (2:260), so that his heart may be at rest.

outline.heading: No question this time, and a son's consent
outline.gist: This time he asks nothing. He tells his son of the vision and asks his view, and the boy, old enough to understand it as revelation, tells him to do as commanded (37:102).

outline.heading: When they both submitted: the word Muslim is coined
outline.gist: The next verse says 'when they both submitted' (37:103); he presents this as the moment the name Muslim was coined, because both fully submitted to a command whose wisdom they could not see.

outline.heading: Shaytan's three attempts
outline.gist: On the way to Mina Shaytan tries Ibrahim, then the 13-year-old Ismail, then Hajar; each drives him off with seven pebbles. In the Quran's eyes a 13-year-old is accountable and capable of carrying the deen, whatever the world says.

outline.heading: Held down, and the knife that would not cut
outline.gist: Ismail asks to be tied down face away so his father does not falter. Ibrahim sharpens the knife and strikes, with no bluff at any step; the knife does not cut, and some narrations say he tried again.

outline.heading: The call and the great ransom
outline.gist: A voice tells Ibrahim he has fulfilled the vision; this was the clear trial, and Allah ransomed Ismail with a great sacrifice, having no interest in his blood (37:104-107). So we spend these days magnifying and glorifying Allah.

outline.heading: Why we celebrate, and why we should not complain
outline.gist: Eid celebrates that Allah never gave us a senseless command. Complaining about hijab, girlfriends or alcohol is audacity toward the One who set safety barriers out of care; we sacrifice and feed the poor to remind ourselves.

outline.heading: Submission includes standing for justice
outline.gist: The same purposeful commands tell us to stand for justice and speak against oppression. Turning a blind eye to others' suffering ultimately harms ourselves.

outline.heading: Interlude
We have grown vain
outline.gist: Arguing with Allah that a command was not helpful treats Him as a peer. It is only His compassion that made every command benefit us, with reward on top, and that should humble us.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: The wisdom and purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: Allah's commands are reasoned and aimed at our best interest by His own choice; He proves it by contrast with the one useless command given to the Israelites, and He rewards obedience on top.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger: religious adherence
themes.note: Ibrahim and Ismail model full submission to a command whose wisdom they could not see; that moment is when the word Muslim was coined, and it leaves us no argument for disobeying commands that plainly help us.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Musa and the repentance of the Israelites after the golden calf, told as Allah's lesson that His commands were otherwise all for their benefit.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: A detailed retelling of Ibrahim's vision, his character as a critical thinker who even asked to see resurrection, Ismail's maturity and consent, and Shaytan's three failed attempts.

themes.label: Hajj, Umrah and Arafah
themes.note: The days of Dhul Hijjah and Eid al-Adha are spent in takbir and sacrifice to celebrate that Allah never commanded anything senseless; the stoning rite recalls the rejection of Shaytan.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Questioning Allah's commands as if negotiating with an equal is vanity; the fact that every command benefits us should humble us.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Commands to stand for justice and speak against oppression also serve us; turning a blind eye to others' suffering ultimately harms ourselves.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: A 13-year-old is accountable and capable of carrying the deen in the Quran's eyes, whatever the world says about being a kid.

quran.point: Had Allah decreed that they kill themselves or leave their homes, only a few would have obeyed; the opening fact of the khutbah.
Musa tells his people they wronged themselves with the calf and must repent by killing one another: the one command with no benefit to them.
This life is play and distraction; Allah does not ask for all your wealth, since that would expose your stinginess.
Allah wants ease for you, not hardship.
He chose you and placed no hardship upon you in the deen.
Ibrahim asks to see how Allah gives life to the dead so his heart may be at rest: evidence that he was a questioner.
Ibrahim tells his son of the vision and asks his view; Ismail tells him to do as commanded.
When they both submitted: the moment he says coined the word Muslim.
The call that Ibrahim fulfilled the vision, that this was the clear trial, and the ransom with a great sacrifice.

hadith.gist: Shaytan appeared to Ibrahim, then Ismail, then Hajar to talk them out of the sacrifice, and each drove him off with seven pebbles, the origin of the stoning of the jamarat.
Some narrations say the knife did not cut on the first stroke, so Ibrahim tried again before the call came.
The Prophet taught that these days are to be spent magnifying and glorifying Allah (takbir, tahmid, tasbih).

maxims: He could have, but He didn't
Every command is reasoned and purposed for your interest
Pure submission. Actual Islam in motion.
Because we love them, we align their interest with reward
You're not speaking to a peer or an equal

stories.who: The Israelites after the golden calf
stories.point: Allah gave them a command that only harmed them, then lifted it and revived them, so they would realise all His other commands were for their good.

stories.who: Ibrahim and Ismail at Mina
stories.point: A man who questioned everything obeyed a command with no visible wisdom without a word; that is the purest submission and the birth of the name Muslim.

stories.who: Shaytan's three attempts on Ibrahim, Ismail and Hajar
stories.point: All three refused him and stoned him; even a 13-year-old understood and held to Allah's command.

contemporary: Young people's complaints about hijab, alcohol and not having girlfriends
takeaways: Before complaining about a religious restriction, remember Allah only commanded what benefits you and rewards you for it.
Approach Allah's commands with submission, not as a negotiation between equals.
Spend the days of Dhul Hijjah in takbir and praise, and mark Eid by sacrificing and feeding the poor in gratitude.
Stand for justice and speak against oppression; ignoring others' suffering harms us too.
Treat teenagers, and let them see themselves, as accountable carriers of the deen.

22:27.ar: وَأَذِّن فِي ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَجِّ يَأۡتُوكَ رِجَالࣰ ا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرࣲ يَأۡتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقࣲ‏
22:27.en: And proclaim unto mankind the pilgrimage. They will come unto thee on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep ravine

2:125.ar: وَإِذۡ جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡبَيۡتَ مَثَابَةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمۡنࣰ ا وَٱتَّخِذُواْ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ مُصَلࣰّ ىۖ وَعَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيۡتِيَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلۡعَٰكِفِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ
2:125.en: And when We made the House (at Makka) a resort for mankind and sanctuary, (saying): Take as your place of worship the place where Abraham stood (to pray). And We imposed a duty upon Abraham and Ishmael, (saying): Purify My house for those who go around and those who meditate therein and those who bow down and prostrate themselves (in worship)

2:158.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:158.en: Lo! (the mountains) As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the indications of Allah. It is therefore no sin for him who is on pilgrimage to the House (of Allah) or visiteth it, to go around them (as the pagan custom is). And he who doeth good of his own accord, (for him) lo! Allah is Responsive, Aware

2:198.ar: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتࣲ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
2:198.en: It is no sin for you that ye seek the bounty of your Lord (by trading). But, when ye press on in the multitude from 'Arafat, remember Allah by the sacred monument. Remember Him as He hath guided you, although before ye were of those astray

9:3.ar: وَأَذَٰنࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحَجِّ ٱلۡأَكۡبَرِ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَرِيٓءࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ وَرَسُولُهُۥۚ فَإِن تُبۡتُمۡ فَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۖ وَإِن تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ فَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّكُمۡ غَيۡرُ مُعۡجِزِي ٱللَّهِۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
9:3.en: And a proclamation from Allah and His messenger to all men on the day of the Greater Pilgrimage that Allah is free from obligation to the idolaters, and (so is) His messenger. So, if ye repent, it will be better for you; but if ye are averse, then know that ye cannot escape Allah. Give tidings (O Muhammad) of a painful doom to those who disbelieve

49:10.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ إِخۡوَةࣱ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَ أَخَوَيۡكُمۡۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
49:10.en: The believers are naught else than brothers. Therefore make peace between your brethren and observe your duty to Allah that haply ye may obtain mercy

9:36.ar: إِنَّ عِدَّةَ ٱلشُّهُورِ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱثۡنَا عَشَرَ شَهۡرࣰ ا فِي كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ يَوۡمَ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ مِنۡهَآ أَرۡبَعَةٌ حُرُمࣱۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُۚ فَلَا تَظۡلِمُواْ فِيهِنَّ أَنفُسَكُمۡۚ وَقَٰتِلُواْ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ كَآفَّةࣰ كَمَا يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمۡ كَآفَّةࣰۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
9:36.en: Lo! the number of the months with Allah is twelve months by Allah's ordinance in the day that He created the heavens and the earth. Four of them are sacred: that is the right religion. So wrong not yourselves in them. And wage war on all of the idolaters as they are waging war on all of you. And know that Allah is with those who keep their duty (unto Him)

4:34.ar: ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٰمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡۚ فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ قَٰنِتَٰتٌ حَٰفِظَٰتࣱ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱلَّٰتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّۖ فَإِنۡ أَطَعۡنَكُمۡ فَلَا تَبۡغُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ سَبِيلًاۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
4:34.en: Men are in charge of women, because Allah hath made the one of them to excel the other, and because they spend of their property (for the support of women). So good women are the obedient, guarding in secret that which Allah hath guarded. As for those from whom ye fear rebellion, admonish them and banish them to beds apart, and scourge them. Then if they obey you, seek not a way against them. Lo! Allah is ever High, Exalted, Great

49:13.en: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

40:19.ar: يَعۡلَمُ خَآئِنَةَ ٱلۡأَعۡيُنِ وَمَا تُخۡفِي ٱلصُّدُورُ
40:19.en: He knoweth the traitor of the eyes, and that which the bosoms hide

lHgTqZAsq24.title: The Farewell Hajj and the Farewell Sermon
lHgTqZAsq24.one_line: Walking through Jabir's long hadith on the Prophet's only Hajj, then the Farewell Sermon's teachings on sanctity, jahiliyyah, women, equality and family.
lHgTqZAsq24.summary: Taking the third line of his Hajj series, he follows the Prophet's single Hajj through Jabir's long narration in Sahih Muslim, avoiding the fiqh disputes and drawing lessons instead. He dwells on Jabir's memory of a sea of people around the Prophet while revelation came down, on the Prophet letting people use their own talbiyahs and easing whatever was not essential, and on the contrast between his lonely call from Safa twenty years earlier and the crowds now repeating his dhikr. Leaving the haram for Arafah ended Quraysh's claim to privilege. He then reads the Farewell Sermon piece by piece: human blood, wealth and honour are more sacred than the holiest day, month and city; all jahiliyyah lies under the Prophet's feet, so every pilgrim must kill his own; Shaytan settles for small sins; women must be treated with taqwa; no race is above another except by taqwa, which only Allah can see, so no one may assign people to Hell; inheritance must be honoured; and the Book of Allah keeps us from straying. He laments confusion over gender roles, delayed marriage, racism among Arabs and inheritance injustice, and urges learning religion from scholars in person.

outline.heading: Opening
The Prophet's only Hajj
outline.gist: One Hajj in year ten, about three months before his death in Rabi' al-Awwal.

outline.heading: A farewell and his first peaceful entry into Makkah
outline.gist: Every earlier visit came by treaty or conquest; this time he entered like anyone else and said goodbye to his ummah and the House.

outline.heading: Jabir's long hadith in Muslim
outline.gist: Long narrations are rarely authentic; Jabir's account of the Hajj is one of the few, narrated in full only by Muslim.

outline.heading: Muhammad al-Baqir visits the blind Jabir
outline.gist: Jabir, poor and old, greets the Prophet's descendant warmly and leads prayer in a tiny garment; he stresses that the imams of Ahl al-Bayt belong to Ahl al-Sunnah too.

outline.heading: The miqats and the prayer that hearts turn toward the House
outline.gist: After naming the miqats the Prophet faced the horizon and asked Allah to turn people's hearts toward them, a prayer answered in today's crowds.

outline.heading: Nine years without Hajj
outline.gist: Barred from the House while the Arabs still went every year, the Muslims felt the loss deeply until the Prophet called people to Hajj in year ten.

outline.heading: Everyone rushes to Madinah to follow him
outline.gist: People dropped everything for the chance to perform Hajj behind the Prophet himself, which no guided group today can match.

outline.heading: Asma bint Umays and how marriage has changed
outline.gist: She married Ja'far, Abu Bakr and Ali in turn; marriage was easier then because people sought religion and character, while today men chase looks and women chase money.

outline.heading: Hajj during postpartum bleeding
outline.gist: Asma gave birth at Dhul-Hulayfah and was told to bathe, protect herself and enter ihram; menstruation and nifas do not prevent Hajj.

outline.heading: Why Jabir knew the Hajj best
outline.gist: He held the reins of the Prophet's camel and never left his side, so his account is usually preferred.

outline.heading: A sea of people with the Prophet among them
outline.gist: Jabir saw crowds in every direction while revelation came down and they did whatever he did; for a lover of the Prophet nothing in life matched those moments.

outline.heading: The talbiyah: he did not force his wording on anyone
outline.gist: He kept his own talbiyah and let others use theirs; he was strict only in the pillars and eased everything else, unlike those who later narrowed it.

outline.heading: Three ways to perform Hajj
outline.gist: Ifrad, tamattu' and qiran, and when a sacrifice is required.

outline.heading: Tawaf and prayer behind Maqam Ibrahim
outline.gist: Touching the Black Stone, brisk walking for three rounds, then two rak'ahs with Al-Kafirun and Al-Ikhlas.

outline.heading: On Safa with the Ansar at his feet
outline.gist: He began where Allah began, declared tawhid and made dua three times while the Ansar said amin.

outline.heading: Safa then and twenty years later
outline.gist: Once he stood alone there and was mocked by Abu Lahab; now multitudes echoed his dhikr. Success comes only after sacrifice.

outline.heading: The sa'i between Safa and Marwa
outline.gist: Hurrying in the valley bed and repeating the dhikr on Marwa.

outline.heading: Had I known beforehand I would not have brought the sacrifice
outline.gist: Those without a sacrificial animal were told to make it an umrah; he takes the view that the Prophet performed qiran.

outline.heading: Suraqa asks: for this year or forever?
outline.gist: The man who once chased him to kill him now follows him; umrah joined with Hajj is permanent, something the Arabs had never known.

outline.heading: Ali objects to Fatimah leaving ihram
outline.gist: Ali came from Yemen with the sacrificial camels and found Fatimah out of ihram; the Prophet confirmed she was right and told Ali to stay in ihram as he had intended Hajj like him.

outline.heading: The Day of Tarwiyah, Mina and the tent at Namirah
outline.gist: He prayed five prayers at Mina, then moved on at sunrise toward Arafah.

outline.heading: Leaving the haram: ending Quraysh's privilege
outline.gist: Quraysh, calling themselves al-Hums, stood only at Muzdalifah inside the haram to set themselves above other Arabs; the Prophet went on to Arafah and abolished that distinction.

outline.heading: The Farewell Sermon and why it carries that name
outline.gist: He spoke on several days so all could hear; he has gathered all its parts into one text.

outline.heading: Perhaps I will not meet you after this year
outline.gist: His opening words made the companions weep.

outline.heading: Mu'adh told he may pass the Prophet's grave
outline.gist: My allies are the God-conscious wherever they are; by the time Mu'adh came back from Yemen the Prophet had died.

outline.heading: What day, month and land is this?
outline.gist: Repeating a question three times was a polite way of signalling that the answer missed the point.

outline.heading: Blood, wealth and honour are more sacred than Arafah
outline.gist: Sanctity upon sanctity surrounded them, yet a person's life, property and honour are holier still; honour your brother as you honour the Kaaba.

outline.heading: No parent wrongs a child, no child a parent
outline.gist: No one is exempt, not even family who take each other's things casually; wealth is lawful only with the owner's goodwill.

outline.heading: Have I conveyed? The point he repeated everywhere
outline.gist: Violating someone's body, wealth or honour cancels any amount of tawaf and umrah.

outline.heading: All of jahiliyyah under my feet
outline.gist: Old blood feuds and usury abolished, starting with his own family's claims; Hajj celebrates the death of jahiliyyah.

outline.heading: Kill your own jahiliyyah
outline.gist: Everyone has a personal jahiliyyah; Hajj is the time to bury its habits, pride, haram money and speech for good.

outline.heading: The jahiliyyah Arabs would be shocked by us
outline.gist: They had chivalry and courage we lack; those who did not kill their jahiliyyah apostatised after the Prophet's death, while those who did carried Islam.

outline.heading: Shaytan settles for the deeds you belittle
outline.gist: He has given up on idol worship but is content with showing off, pride, anger and stinginess, which lead to worse.

outline.heading: Time has come full circle; do not turn on each other
outline.gist: The sacred months restored to Ibrahim's calendar, and a warning against Muslims striking each other's necks.

outline.heading: The rights of wives and husbands
outline.gist: Fear Allah regarding women, who are entrusted to you by Allah's covenant; a whole section of his final sermon.

outline.heading: One hundred thousand listeners and the relaying riders
outline.gist: He spoke slowly so riders could carry each phrase to the crowd, so a two-minute text took hours.

outline.heading: Our confusion about men's and women's roles
outline.gist: Muslims need a full review of the relationship between men and women; he sees violent men and women who neglect their homes, and whatever he says angers one side.

outline.heading: Young people with money who do not marry
outline.gist: In Syria the poor married young; here wealthy men and women in their thirties keep delaying without reason.

outline.heading: Your Lord is one and your father is one
outline.gist: No Arab over non-Arab or colour over colour except by taqwa, proclaimed where Adam and Ibrahim had stood.

outline.heading: Racism shrinks until only the self remains
outline.gist: Contempt for non-Arabs becomes contempt for other Arabs, other cities, other families, until a person sees merit only in himself.

outline.heading: Taqwa is known only to Allah: do not assign people to Hell
outline.gist: Warn by Allah's words in general, but speaking about named individuals' fates is a frightening boldness.

outline.heading: Hasan al-Basri and the death of al-Hajjaj
outline.gist: Hasan rejoiced at the tyrant's death yet feared that his final words of hope in Allah's forgiveness might earn him mercy.

outline.heading: Knowledge is taken from people, not only books
outline.gist: No doctor or lawyer is made by reading alone; sit with the rabbaniyyun to learn their manners and how they speak about people.

outline.heading: I will be waiting for you at the Hawd
outline.gist: He will rescue some from the Fire, while some will be taken from him for changing the religion after him, keeping only its outward look.

outline.heading: Inheritance and the sanctity of the family
outline.gist: Each heir has a share and lineage must stay honest; inheritance disputes in Middle Eastern courts are endless, like the hundreds of files behind a Damascus judge he knew.

outline.heading: I leave you the Book of Allah
outline.gist: Holding to the Quran, with the Sunnah and respect for his family, keeps the ummah on the straight path.

outline.heading: Let those present tell those absent
outline.gist: A later listener may understand better than the one who heard; the companions wept and testified that he had conveyed the message.

outline.heading: Outro

7:23.en: They said: Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If thou forgive us not and have not mercy on us, surely we are of the lost

22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the endeavour which is His right. He hath chosen you and hath not laid upon you in religion any hardship; the faith of your father Abraham (is yours). He hath named you Muslims of old time and in this (Scripture), that the messenger may be a witness against you, and that ye may be witnesses against mankind. cOyJDat81Tw.title: Arafat Lecture: The Day of Realization
cOyJDat81Tw.one_line: On the Day of Arafah: turning knowledge into realization, celebrating diversity, repenting like Adam, and submitting like Ibrahim to commands that are all for our good.
cOyJDat81Tw.summary: Given on the Day of Arafah, the talk opens with the hadith in which the Prophet listed the rewards of each stage of Hajj, ending with the pilgrim returning sinless like a newborn. Arafah, he argues, is about ma'rifah: the gap between having information and realizing what it means. Adam and Hawwa realized their purpose there, Ibrahim realized his dream was a command, and the Prophet realized his mission was complete and gave the Farewell Sermon on human equality. Reading Al-Hujurat 13 in full, he praises the diversity of his Canadian congregation compared with the masjid of his youth in Syria, and urges people to actually learn each other's names, since knowing people widens the mind. Ignorance spoils everything it mixes with, from power that bombs Gaza to religion, so Muslims can no longer afford to be uneducated. He retells the first repentance and the trial of Ibrahim, imagining how history would have judged him had the knife cut, and concludes that Eid celebrates a merciful Lord whose every command protects us. Young people should move from feeling Islam as a burden to gratitude, as a parent's limits on a tantruming child are mercy.

outline.heading: The man whose question the Prophet answered before he asked
outline.gist: Crowds filled Madinah before the Farewell Hajj and the Prophet, always reachable, told a questioner what he had come to ask to strengthen weak faith.

outline.heading: Reward for every step toward Makkah
outline.gist: Each step of the pilgrim or his mount brings a good deed and removes a sin.

outline.heading: Allah boasts of the dusty pilgrims at Arafah
outline.gist: He forgives them even if their sins outnumber raindrops and grains of sand; he asks that those not there be granted the same.

outline.heading: Stoning, shaving and the final tawaf: a new beginning
outline.gist: Every hair becomes light on the Day of Judgment and the pilgrim returns as on the day he was born.

outline.heading: Arafah: information versus realization
outline.gist: Knowing halal and haram is different from realizing why it matters; Adam had been taught much but only realized his purpose at Arafah.

outline.heading: The Prophet realizes his mission is complete
outline.gist: When the verse of the completed religion came down at Arafah he knew his time was ending, so he gave his final sermon.

outline.heading: The Farewell Sermon on human equality
outline.gist: One Lord, one father, all from soil; colour and race give no advantage.

outline.heading: Why did Allah make us so diverse?
outline.gist: Reading the whole verse: nations and tribes so that you may know one another; would it not be easier if we were all the same?

outline.heading: A masjid where everyone was a Rajeh
outline.gist: He led his first masjid at seventeen in a Syrian village where most worshippers shared his surname and looked alike.

outline.heading: The diversity he fears losing
outline.gist: Here worshippers come from Syria to Sudan to Bosnia to Myanmar, united by Allah and descent from Adam; homogeneous home countries cannot offer this brotherhood.

outline.heading: Ta'aruf, ma'rifah and the name Arafah
outline.gist: Getting to know one another shares a root with ma'rifah, processed knowledge that changes thinking or behaviour; the best day of the year bears that name.

outline.heading: Knowledge at the heart of revelation
outline.gist: The first five verses mention knowledge six times, and the man who explained the first revelation was named Waraqah, paper.

outline.heading: Realizing you were wrong or not doing enough
outline.gist: We return to Adam's spot, or gather here, hoping to realize something about ourselves.

outline.heading: Ignorance spoils everything it touches
outline.gist: Ignorance with power bombs children for six hundred days, with wealth wastes it on haram, with health abuses the body, and with religion is the worst mix.

outline.heading: Muslims can no longer afford to be uneducated
outline.gist: The realization of this day should be that being poorly educated is not an option for a Muslim or the ummah.

outline.heading: Realizations that saved Adam and Ibrahim
outline.gist: Adam's realization saved him and his family; Ibrahim's hard decision is what Eid celebrates.

outline.heading: Praying beside people for years without knowing their names
outline.gist: The Prophet built his message on people knowing each other; meeting others widens the mind and cures narrow-mindedness, even about differences in Islamic law.

outline.heading: Those who know Allah: your potential is limited by your knowledge
outline.gist: Scholars were praised as al-'arifun billah; everyone knows Allah, but not equally.

outline.heading: The first repentance in history
outline.gist: Adam realized his wrong but had no words, so Allah taught him the dua he urges people to make today; every year their children return to be forgiven.

outline.heading: Submission: the main theme of Hajj
outline.gist: Surat al-Hajj ends by naming Ibrahim and the religion he left, one with no hardship.

outline.heading: Ibrahim named you Muslims
outline.gist: The name we take pride in was given by Ibrahim.

outline.heading: Submitting when the command looks only harmful
outline.gist: Obeying is easy when the benefit is visible; Ibrahim saw no wisdom, only horror, and how he would answer to his wife, son and people.

outline.heading: Had the knife cut, would history have forgiven him?
outline.gist: Imagine Ismail had died: Ibrahim would have been remembered as a child killer rather than revered.

outline.heading: Father and son both submit
outline.gist: Ismail answers without hesitation; Ibrahim walks on knowing he may lose his son, his name and everything, and lays him down.

outline.heading: The knife will not cut
outline.gist: He strikes again and again until he is called: you have fulfilled the vision, and a ransom is given.

outline.heading: Eid celebrates the edge of a knife
outline.gist: The line between cutting and not cutting decided whether Ibrahim became the most celebrated person on earth.

outline.heading: Every command is in your best interest
outline.gist: Allah never asked us to do anything harmful; only Ibrahim could bear such a trial, and Allah has no interest in our suffering, so He gave us sacrifice that feeds the poor.

outline.heading: The takbirat of Eid as thanks
outline.gist: The words of these days celebrate Allah's generosity in giving commands aligned with our good.

outline.heading: Our commands protect our own necks
outline.gist: Avoiding intoxicants, chastity, hijab, honesty and hard work all protect us; if we cannot submit when it helps us, we would never submit when it hurts.

outline.heading: From burden to gratitude
outline.gist: He asks the youth how they feel about prayer, zakat and caring for parents: a weight holding them back, or a gift from a completed religion?

outline.heading: A child's tantrum and a merciful parent
outline.gist: His three-year-old melts down when refused candy; Allah looks at our complaints about His commands with the same mercy.

outline.heading: Outro

hU81eHknd2s.title: The Final Sermon, Part 2
hU81eHknd2s.one_line: Paragraph-by-paragraph reading of the Farewell Sermon: sanctity of life, end of Jahiliyyah, Shaytan's patience, unity, women's rights, equality, the basin.
hU81eHknd2s.summary: Second session on the Prophet's Farewell Sermon, delivered on Arafah and repeated during the Hajj. He treats the sermon as the clearest snapshot of the Prophet's legacy because it was given to 100,000 people with no private context to explain it away. After recapping the first paragraph on the sanctity of life, wealth and honour, he works through the rest: Jahiliyyah is under my feet, with the Prophet cancelling his own family's blood feud and his uncle's riba first (a long aside on today's compound-interest economy); Shaytan has given up on idols but is content with small, gradual disobedience, so the struggle is not over; return to Ibrahim's basics and do not draw swords on each other after I die, which becomes a call to unity and a demand that every listener hunt down and kill the racism he absorbed at home; a full paragraph on the rights of wives, which he reads as the foundation of the ummah being its households and the loss of a balanced, non-political conversation about marriage roles; your Lord is one and your father is one, so only taqwa distinguishes people, and racism is just collective arrogance; I am waiting for you at the basin, and some will be turned away for what they changed after him; inheritance protects the family; convey this to the absent, because later generations will understand more; and finally, hold on to the Book of Allah, you will be asked about me. He ends with the crowd's reply and the Prophet's tears.

outline.heading: Opening
Paragraph one recap: people above holy places
outline.gist: He gave the sermon on Arafah at the mount of mercy, again on the day of sacrifice and through the days after, at least three times as Imam Ahmad notes, choosing paragraphs each time but always repeating the first: the Kaaba, Arafah, Dhul-Hijjah and Makkah are holy, but the sanctity of the person beside you is greater.

outline.heading: A legacy that could not be used to shed blood
outline.gist: He had just been told his time was near and knew he would never again address so many, so he made sure no one could use his teaching to kill, oppress or transgress. It happened anyway, but he cannot be blamed for it.

outline.heading: Lost in the peripheries, numb to bloodshed
outline.gist: Taking life's sanctity seriously also shapes how you react to those who violate it. Caught up in tertiary arguments, Muslims have drifted from that essence: they watch Muslims massacred with a mellow, empty reaction, while fundamentalists in their own ranks shed Muslim blood lightly.

outline.heading: The sermon as a public snapshot of his legacy
outline.gist: Grasping someone's legacy takes wisdom and maturity; thrown into the ocean of narrations without scholarly guidance you drown. Much of what he said was circumstantial, but a sermon to 100,000 people has no context to explain it away.

outline.heading: Paragraph two: Jahiliyyah is under my feet
outline.gist: He recites the second paragraph: everything of Jahiliyyah is abolished, its blood claims and its riba. That day he slaughtered the livestock of Jahiliyyah on the mountain, ending its financial and social system.

outline.heading: The infant of Banu Sa'd: his own family's feud first
outline.gist: The first blood he cancelled was that of Ibn Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith, his cousin's infant son, killed in a raid while being nursed among Banu Sa'd, which had set off a feud of about fifteen deaths. He started with his own family.

outline.heading: Riba cancelled, starting with al-Abbas
outline.gist: The first riba cancelled was his uncle al-Abbas's: lenders take back their capital, no one oppressed either way. Today's compounding debt, where whole countries become the collateral, is a system a five-year-old would find absurd; no financial advisor has given him a sensible answer, and as in medicine, where he rechecks the radiologist, you must question the status quo.

outline.heading: Bury Jahiliyyah: those who did began a new era
outline.gist: He ended the bigotry, racism, corruption and vengeance of Jahiliyyah: get over yourselves and move into the future. Some who heard him apostatized three months later; those who buried it began an era Muslims barely study, while non-Muslims often know our history better and we read it as a political fight.

outline.heading: Paragraph three: Shaytan settles for small things
outline.gist: Shaytan has despaired of being worshipped through idols in this land, but is content to be obeyed in deeds you think small: a little haram, a glance now and then, then he leaves you for fifteen years. He is in no hurry.

outline.heading: Sins come in steps, years apart
outline.gist: No one living in purity suddenly falls into zina or theft. Shaytan moves you a step, keeps you there for years, then another step a decade later, until tipping over is easy.

outline.heading: A little riya until your whims are your lord
outline.gist: He does not need open shirk: a little showing off, bathing in people's approval, then a few choices of reputation over sincerity, until your lord is your whims, or a god reshaped to suit them.

outline.heading: Shaytan the lawyer
outline.gist: He is educated and knows Allah's law inside out after millennia; if one approach fails he finds another and builds the case to a sentence you cannot beat. Without awareness and caution you have no chance.

outline.heading: The struggle is not over
outline.gist: Toppling the idols around the Kaaba did not end it: Shaytan compromises, and if he cannot get full shirk he takes the next best thing.

outline.heading: Shirk proven by conduct, not confession
outline.gist: Like a lawyer, he need not get a confession; if your actions are consistent with worshipping a person or your whims, saying you never claimed shirk is a criminal's plea of not guilty.

outline.heading: Imagine him leaving you: his parting advice
outline.gist: Hear these words as if you had lived a lifetime with him and he was going away: take the sanctity of others as seriously as your own, and let everything Jahiliyyah stood for die.

outline.heading: Virtues of Jahiliyyah we have lost
outline.gist: Some who died in Jahiliyyah would ask us where our taqwa is: they had basic decency, bravery, commitment to a cause and truthfulness to their word. Abu Jahl was more committed to shirk than half-in, half-out Muslims are to Islam.

outline.heading: Paragraph four: back to Ibrahim's basics
outline.gist: Time has returned to how Allah created it, with the sacred months in their places: drop the futile tertiary arguments and return to the simple basics everyone agrees on, which predate him.

outline.heading: Do not draw swords on each other after I die
outline.gist: He asked for unity: do not regress after him to putting swords on your brothers' necks over differences you could overlook. Muslims fell into every trap he named, unleashing their most vicious side on other Muslims.

outline.heading: The ummah has not hit bottom; its peaks came from unity
outline.gist: Until Muslims value unity over being right, the decline continues, and there is room to fall further. Every historical peak came from leaders who put a cause and unity above personal differences and brought together peoples who did not like each other.

outline.heading: Displacement taught Muslim peoples to know each other
outline.gist: The tragedies of recent decades scattered Palestinians, Iraqis, Lebanese, Syrians, Somalis and Sudanese into each other's countries; Turks came to know Syrians, Iraqis to know Palestinians, and knowing one another helps sheathe the swords.

outline.heading: Fifteen countries in one room
outline.gist: He united 100,000 unarmed people who did not like each other; a room of fifty here spans fifteen countries listening to a Syrian, despite stereotypes and real grievances (he jokes that Lebanese resentment of Syrians is earned). Diversity should be heartwarming, and because most companions held together after him, Islam spread.

outline.heading: If you never remove racism, you are racist
outline.gist: You absorbed talk about certain groups at home; 'I like everyone, just not those people' is racism. Find it, neutralize it, kill it. After each statement he asked 'have I conveyed?', riders carried it through the crowd, and he called Allah to witness.

outline.heading: Paragraph five, the longest: fear Allah regarding women
outline.gist: After sanctity, the end of Jahiliyyah, the ongoing struggle and unity, he chose to spend his longest paragraph on the rights of women and how the Arabs must treat them better, as people and partners in building the nation.

outline.heading: Wives are a trust under Allah's covenant
outline.gist: Men brought their wives home by Allah's decree and covenant; He is their guardian, and whoever mistreats them answers to Him directly. Anyone raising this in such a sermon today would be called whitewashed.

outline.heading: The ummah is just its households
outline.gist: He knew the nation could only stand on strong households with clear rights, both spouses contributing. The ummah of Muhammad is nothing but its collective households; rights run both ways and he was biased to neither side.

outline.heading: Women made equal in accountability and rights
outline.gist: The pendulum had already swung against women in a patriarchal desert society built around survival. Islam made them equally accountable, with the same reward and punishment, and gave them ownership, business, choice of spouse and inheritance.

outline.heading: The lost middle ground
outline.gist: This conversation is more pressing than ever because the balance is gone: the rhetoric is politicized and unhealthy for both sexes, and the longer it lasts the more the next generation's marriages are delayed, unhappy and weak.

outline.heading: Men: providers and protectors
outline.gist: The issue is the nature of the household, not the number of children. Men must understand their wife is an amanah, as one day you will ask your own daughter's husband to care for her after you die: patient, kind, generous, never ruled by temper.

outline.heading: Women: the emotional protectors of the home
outline.gist: Women too must learn what it means to be a wife: nurturer and emotional protector of the house. A man not supported and respected at home is weak outside, and a weak man is useless; spouses should not compete, since each one's success belongs to the household.

outline.heading: Paragraph six: your Lord is one, your father is one
outline.gist: An unparalleled statement of human equality: all are from Adam and Adam from dust; no Arab over non-Arab, no red over black, except by taqwa, followed by 49:13. Origin, colour, wealth, age, health and size make no difference.

outline.heading: Saved for the spot where Adam and Eve reunited
outline.gist: The line appears nowhere else; he seems to have held it for the mount where Adam and Eve came together again, before a crowd from every walk of life, so it would land and stick.

outline.heading: Taqwa has no barometer
outline.gist: Taqwa is the only advantage and it sits in the heart; no blood test measures it, so ranking anyone above another rests on ignorance and you will answer for it.

outline.heading: Racism is collective arrogance
outline.gist: Arrogance is thinking you are better than one person; racism is thinking you are better than everyone like him. A ruler's heir and a foundling left by a dumpster cannot be ranked: merit is taqwa alone, judged later.

outline.heading: What about the non-Muslim? Worry about your own taqwa
outline.gist: Do you know how much taqwa you will have on the day you die? Only someone strangely confident about his own would look at others; he would like to shop at that market.

outline.heading: One big family
outline.gist: The sermon makes humanity one family, a miserable one like every family, in which no one is better or lesser and everyone is there to support, empower and help the others forward.

outline.heading: Paragraph seven: I am waiting for you at the basin
outline.gist: A personal statement: he waits at the basin hoping to show off the numbers of his ummah, so do not make him look bad by failing to keep your side of the deal. He will intercede and pull people from the punishment.

outline.heading: Familiar faces turned away
outline.gist: Some he tries to save will be taken from him; he will say they are his, familiar faces who prayed, and be told he does not know what they changed after him. They dressed like him but hollowed his values and practice into empty skeletons.

outline.heading: Our appointment is the basin
outline.gist: Life is too busy for visits and dinners: our appointment is the basin. Make it that far and the rest will be taken care of; he hopes none of us is taken away.

outline.heading: Paragraph eight: inheritance and lineage protect the family
outline.gist: Everyone receives his share of inheritance, no one is cut out or takes more, and no one claims or is removed from a family not his own, all to protect the sanctity of the family.

outline.heading: Sisters cut out of inheritance in his village
outline.gist: As a child he did not see why this was in the sermon; then in his village he watched brothers manipulate parents to deprive sisters and each other, and outsiders gain more influence over a father than his children and tear kin apart.

outline.heading: Paragraph nine: convey to the absent
outline.gist: Let the one present convey it to the absent, for many who are told later will understand it more deeply than those who heard it, and many will carry knowledge to people more knowledgeable than themselves; he uses this line often in arguments.

outline.heading: The completed religion grows like a tree
outline.gist: He built his teaching to last: with 'today I have completed your religion' (5:3) there is no new revelation, so everything is handed forward and will make more sense to later people. Carry what you do not understand and pass it on; some will understand the companions' reports better than the companions.

outline.heading: Hind bint Utbah's pledge
outline.gist: At the end of his life Hind, Abu Sufyan's wife, objected during her pledge that a free woman would never commit zina; he smiled and told her simply to pledge, because the pledge was for centuries to come, when it would not be so clear-cut.

outline.heading: A teacher fails if his students don't surpass him
outline.gist: Each generation must know more than the one before or the tree of knowledge shrinks: Sahih Muslim grew into 25 volumes of commentary. We can never have the companions' piety, having missed that moment, but we can know more, and that is why we are here.

outline.heading: Final paragraph: hold to the Book of Allah
outline.gist: I have left you that which, if you hold to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah.

outline.heading: You will be asked about me
outline.gist: You will meet your Lord and be asked about me; what will you say? The confused crowd took it up until 100,000 voices shouted that he had conveyed, exhausted himself and given everything, as he stood with tears asking Allah to witness.

outline.heading: Who has a green card not to be worried?
outline.gist: If he was worried about how he did his job and needed to hear it from them, no one has grounds to feel secure. Allah will ask us how he did; then He will ask him about us.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: The whole lecture is a reading of the Farewell Sermon as the Prophet's chosen legacy statement, given publicly with no private context, three months before his death.

themes.label: The unlawfulness of harm and protecting others
themes.note: The sanctity of a person's blood, wealth and honour outranks the sanctity of Makkah, Arafah and the sacred months; a Muslim neither takes life lightly nor lets others do so, and reacts to oppression accordingly.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Fundamentalists within Muslim ranks who shed Muslim blood have missed the essence of the legacy; grasping a legacy needs maturity and scholarly guidance so you do not drown in the ocean of narrations.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Abolishing riba, starting with Abbas's loans, is contrasted with today's compounding-debt system where whole countries become the collateral; he calls it unsustainable and says financial advisors gave him no sensible answer.

themes.label: Shaytan: his methods and defending against him
themes.note: Shaytan no longer hopes for idol worship but is satisfied with small obedience he can grow over decades; he is a lawyer who knows Allah's law and convicts you through conduct consistent with shirk. Be cautious for your deen; the struggle is not over.

themes.label: Sins, their causes and remedies
themes.note: Nobody falls into zina or theft suddenly; it comes in steps years apart. A little riya, kept up long enough, ends with your whims as your lord and a god reshaped to suit them.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Do not regress after I die and put swords to your brothers' necks. The ummah has not hit rock bottom; its peaks came from leaders who put a cause and unity over personal differences, and a room of 15 nationalities listening to a Syrian is proof the message can still unite.

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Displacement taught Muslim peoples to know each other. Everyone carries racism absorbed from parents; you must take time to find it and kill it, or you are racist without knowing. Diversity should be heartwarming, not grounds for superiority.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Wives are taken by Allah's covenant and He is their guardian; the ummah is just its collective households, so the Prophet spent his longest paragraph on treating women well. Men must understand provider and protector roles; women must be the home's emotional protector; the current conversation is politicized and unbalanced, delaying and weakening marriages.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty
themes.note: Islam made women equal in accountability, reward and punishment, and gave them ownership, business, choice of spouse and inheritance, none of which was the norm in Arabia.

themes.label: Taqwa and God-consciousness
themes.note: Taqwa is the only merit that ranks people, and it sits in the heart where no one can measure it, so no one may claim superiority; the question 'what about the non-Muslim' is redirected to how much taqwa you will have the day you die.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Racism is collective arrogance, arrogance times a million; a foundling by a dumpster and a ruler's heir cannot be ranked.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The Prophet waits at the basin hoping to boast of his followers and to intercede; some familiar faces are turned away because they hollowed out his teaching into empty skeletons after him.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Inheritance and lineage rules protect the sanctity of the family; he saw brothers deprive sisters and outsiders capture a father's wealth and tear kin apart.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Convey to the absent, for those told later may understand more than those who heard: knowledge is a growing tree. Our generation must know more than its teachers or it has failed them, since we cannot share the companions' moment but can surpass their knowledge.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The one thing he left behind: hold to the Book of Allah and you will never go astray.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: Having given everything, he still needed to hear from the people that he had done his job, and wept as they shouted it; if he was worried about his performance, no one has a licence not to be.

quran.point: He says the Prophet had 'just received his obituary' and knew he would not live long; the surah is not named but this is the standard reference.
The Prophet recites that the most honoured before Allah is the one with most taqwa, grounding the statement that no race or lineage carries merit.
'Today I have completed your religion for you' was heard on that day; no other faith has such a verse, so everything taught is handed forward with nothing to add.

hadith.gist: Farewell Sermon, paragraph one: your blood, wealth and honour are as sacred to one another as this day, this month and this land.
hadith.source: Farewell Sermon (he notes Imam Ahmad records it being delivered at least three times)

hadith.gist: Paragraph two: everything of Jahiliyyah is under my feet; its blood claims are abolished, the first I cancel is the blood of Ibn Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith; its riba is abolished, the first I cancel is the riba of al-Abbas, you keep only your capital.
Paragraph three: Shaytan has despaired of being worshipped in your land, but he is content to be obeyed in things you consider small; so be cautious of him for your deen.

Paragraph four: time has returned to its original form as on the day Allah created the heavens and earth, with the sacred months in their places; do not return after me to striking each other's necks.
After each statement the Prophet asked 'have I conveyed?', riders carried his words through the crowd, the people affirmed, and he said 'O Allah, be witness'.
Paragraph five: fear Allah regarding women; you took them by the trust of Allah and made them lawful by His word; they have rights over you and you over them; my advice is to treat them well.
Paragraph six: O people, your Lord is one and your father is one; you are all from Adam and Adam is from dust; no Arab over non-Arab, no red over black, except by taqwa.

Paragraph seven: I am waiting for you at the basin and I will boast of your numbers before the nations; some I will try to save will be taken from me, I will say 'my companions', and be told you do not know what they changed after you; then he will say 'away with them'.
Paragraph eight: inheritance shares and lineage must be preserved; no one is cut out, no one takes more than his share, and no one claims a family that is not his.

Paragraph nine: let the one present convey to the absent; perhaps one who is told will understand it better than the one who heard it, and many will carry knowledge to people more knowledgeable than themselves.
Hind bint Utbah, at her pledge, objected 'would a free woman commit zina?'; the Prophet smiled and told her to simply give the pledge, legislating for later generations.

Final paragraph: I have left among you that which, if you hold to it, you will never go astray, the Book of Allah; you will meet your Lord and be asked about me, what will you say? They said: you conveyed, fulfilled and advised; he raised his finger to the sky, 'O Allah, be witness'.

maxims: The ummah of Muhammad is just the collective households
Racism is just collective arrogance
If you don't take time to remove racism, you are racist
A weak man is useless
Jahiliyyah has to die
Who here has a green card not to be worried?

stories.who: The infant son of the Prophet's cousin Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith, killed in a raid while nursing among Banu Sa'd, and the blood feud that followed
stories.point: The Prophet ended Jahiliyyah's vengeance by cancelling his own family's claim first; leaders bury their own grievances before asking others to.

stories.who: Abbas's loans cancelled to capital only
stories.point: Riba ended with the Prophet's own uncle; contrasted with a modern system where the debtor can never reach the capital.

stories.who: Attendees who apostatized three months after the sermon
stories.point: Some who heard him were not ready to bury Jahiliyyah; those who did began a new era that Muslims barely study.

stories.who: Displaced Palestinians, Iraqis, Lebanese, Syrians, Somalis and Sudanese
stories.point: The tragedies of recent decades scattered Muslims into each other's countries, and knowing one another makes it possible to put the swords back.

stories.who: A Syrian imam teaching Turks and Lebanese in a 15-country room
stories.point: Stereotypes and real grievances exist (he jokes the Syrian army earned Lebanese resentment), yet the message brings people who would never listen to each other into one room.

stories.who: Adam and Eve reuniting on the mount of mercy
stories.point: The Prophet seems to have saved his one-sentence declaration of human equality for the spot and crowd where it would land and be remembered.

stories.who: Sisters deprived of inheritance in his home village
stories.point: Watching brothers manipulate parents and outsiders capture a father's wealth showed him why the Prophet spent part of his last sermon on inheritance.

stories.who: Hind bint Utbah's pledge
stories.point: What was unthinkable to a noblewoman of her day would not stay unthinkable; the Prophet legislated for centuries, not for the person in front of him.

stories.who: Sahih Muslim and its 25 volumes of commentary
stories.point: Knowledge is meant to grow with each generation; a teacher whose students do not surpass him has failed.

stories.who: 100,000 people shouting that he had conveyed the message, and his tears
stories.point: The Prophet himself needed to hear that he had done his job; none of us has grounds to feel secure about ours.

contemporary: Muslims massacred around the globe while the Muslim reaction stays mellow and desensitized; fundamentalists within Muslim ranks shedding Muslim blood
The modern compound-interest debt system in which countries become the collateral; financial advisors who could not answer his questions; questioning the status quo as he does in medicine
Mass displacement of Palestinians, Iraqis, Lebanese, Syrians, Somalis and Sudanese into Turkey, the Gulf and elsewhere as an unintended path to mutual understanding
About 50 attendees from roughly 15 countries in the room; Syrian, Turkish and Lebanese stereotypes and the Syrian army's record in Lebanon

Politically driven, unbalanced rhetoric about men's and women's roles; delayed marriages and weaker families in the upcoming generation; the 'whitewashed' accusation thrown at anyone raising women's rights
Non-Muslims knowing Islamic history better than Muslims, who read it only as a political fight
takeaways: Treat every person's life, wealth and honour as a red line you never cross, and let that shape how you react to those who do
Guard against Shaytan's small, patient steps (a little haram, a little showing off) rather than only the big sins
Put the unity of the ummah above being right, and deliberately search out and neutralize the racism you absorbed growing up
Husbands: treat your wife as a trust from Allah and be her provider and protector; wives: be the home's emotional protector; stop competing with each other
Judge no one's taqwa, hold on to the Quran, pass on what you learn so the next generation knows more, and make it to the basin

22:27.ar: وَأَذِّن فِي ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَجِّ يَأۡتُوكَ رِجَالࣰ ا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرࣲ يَأۡتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقࣲ‏
22:27.en: And proclaim unto mankind the pilgrimage. They will come unto thee on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep ravine

2:67.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُكُمۡ أَن تَذۡبَحُواْ بَقَرَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوࣰ اۖ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
2:67.en: And when Moses said unto his people: Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye sacrifice a cow, they said: Dost thou make game of us? He answered: Allah forbid that I should be among the foolish

2:68.ar: قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةࣱ لَّا فَارِضࣱ وَلَا بِكۡرٌ عَوَانُۢ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَۖ فَٱفۡعَلُواْ مَا تُؤۡمَرُونَ
2:68.en: They said: Pray for us unto thy Lord that He make clear to us what (cow) she is. (Moses) answered: Lo! He saith, Verily she is a cow neither with calf nor immature; (she is) between the two conditions; so do that which ye are commanded

2:69.ar: قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوۡنُهَاۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةࣱ صَفۡرَآءُ فَاقِعࣱ لَّوۡنُهَا تَسُرُّ ٱلنَّٰظِرِينَ
2:69.en: They said: Pray for us unto thy Lord that He make clear to us of what colour she is. (Moses) answered: Lo! He saith: Verily she is a yellow cow. Bright is her colour, gladdening beholders

2:70.ar: قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَقَرَ تَشَٰبَهَ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِنَّآ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَمُهۡتَدُونَ
2:70.en: They said: Pray for us unto thy Lord that He make clear to us what (cow) she is. Lo! cows are much alike to us; and Lo! if Allah wills, we may be led aright

2:71.ar: قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةࣱ لَّا ذَلُولࣱ تُثِيرُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَلَا تَسۡقِي ٱلۡحَرۡثَ مُسَلَّمَةࣱ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَاۚ قَالُواْ ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ جِئۡتَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
2:71.en: (Moses) answered: Lo! He saith: Verily she is a cow unyoked; she plougheth not the soil nor watereth the tilth; whole and without mark. They said: Now thou bringest the truth. So they sacrificed her, though almost they did not

2:125.ar: وَإِذۡ جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡبَيۡتَ مَثَابَةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمۡنࣰ ا وَٱتَّخِذُواْ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ مُصَلࣰّ ىۖ وَعَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيۡتِيَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلۡعَٰكِفِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ
2:125.en: And when We made the House (at Makka) a resort for mankind and sanctuary, (saying): Take as your place of worship the place where Abraham stood (to pray). And We imposed a duty upon Abraham and Ishmael, (saying): Purify My house for those who go around and those who meditate therein and those who bow down and prostrate themselves (in worship)

2:158.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:158.en: Lo! (the mountains) As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the indications of Allah. It is therefore no sin for him who is on pilgrimage to the House (of Allah) or visiteth it, to go around them (as the pagan custom is). And he who doeth good of his own accord, (for him) lo! Allah is Responsive, Aware

2:198.ar: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتࣲ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
2:198.en: It is no sin for you that ye seek the bounty of your Lord (by trading). But, when ye press on in the multitude from 'Arafat, remember Allah by the sacred monument. Remember Him as He hath guided you, although before ye were of those astray

2:199.ar: ثُمَّ أَفِيضُواْ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ أَفَاضَ ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:199.en: Then hasten onward from the place whence the multitude hasteneth onward, and ask forgiveness of Allah. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

5:3.ar: حُرِّمَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةُ وَٱلدَّمُ وَلَحۡمُ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ وَٱلۡمُنۡخَنِقَةُ وَٱلۡمَوۡقُوذَةُ وَٱلۡمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيۡتُمۡ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسۡتَقۡسِمُواْ بِٱلۡأَزۡلَٰمِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ فِسۡقٌۗ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمۡ فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِۚ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ أَكۡمَلۡتُ لَكُمۡ دِينَكُمۡ وَأَتۡمَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعۡمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمَ دِينࣰ اۚ فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ فِي مَخۡمَصَةٍ غَيۡرَ مُتَجَانِفࣲ لِّإِثۡمࣲ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
5:3.en: Forbidden unto you (for food) are carrion and blood and swineflesh, and that which hath been dedicated unto any other than Allah, and the strangled, and the dead through beating, and the dead through falling from a height, and that which hath been killed by (the goring of) horns, and the devoured of wild beasts, saving that which ye make lawful (by the death-stroke), and that which hath been immolated unto idols. And (forbidden is it) that ye swear by the divining arrows. This is an abomination. This day are those who disbelieve in despair of (ever harming) your religion; so fear them not, fear Me! This day have I perfected your religion for you and completed My favour unto you, and have chosen for you as religion al-Islam. Whoso is forced by hunger, not by will, to sin: (for him) lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful
